title: WHAT THEY KEPT AND WHAT THEY DESTROYED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites carried off for themselves all the plunder and livestock of these cities, but all the people they put to the sword until they completely destroyed them, not sparing anyone that breathed - Josh 11:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse draws a hard line between what Israel kept and what was destroyed. The plunder and livestock became theirs, but the people were not spared. Once again the text refuses to look away from the cost of God's judgment, and neither should we.

It helps to remember what this moment was and was not. It was the long-delayed judgment of God on a society steeped in evil, carried out through Israel as His instrument at one point in history. It was not a licence for cruelty, a model for how nations should treat one another, or a template for how we treat people who oppose us. The whole tone of the New Testament turns us in a different direction entirely: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, overcome evil with good (Matt 5:44; Rom 12:21).

So what do we carry away from a verse like this? Chiefly a right fear of God and a deep gratitude. The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23) — that is the sober backdrop of every page of the Bible. But the same verse continues, "the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." Israel took plunder from a fallen city; in Christ, we receive an inheritance we never fought for, purchased not by our sword but by His blood (1 Pet 1:18-19).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does this verse deepen your gratitude for the mercy you have received?
- How does Jesus' command to love enemies reshape the way you treat opponents?
- What inheritance in Christ have you received that you could never earn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, the seriousness of sin humbles me. Thank You for the gift of life in Christ that I could never have won for myself. Teach me to love even my enemies. Amen.

cross_references.label: Cross References
cross_references.text:
(Rom 6:23; Matt 5:44; Rom 12:21; 1 Pet 1:18-19)

Note: Like verse 10-11, this is a difficult text of judgment. It is here to make us feel the weight of sin and the wonder of grace, never to license harm toward others.
